meta.title: MiroFish - Predict Everything
meta.description: MiroFish - Social Media Opinion Simulation System

home.heroDesc: From a single document, {brand} extracts reality seeds to auto-generate a parallel world with up to {agentScale}. Inject variables from a god's-eye view to find the {optimalSolution} in complex group dynamics.
home.slogan: Let Agents rehearse the future, let decisions prevail
home.systemReadyDesc: Prediction engine on standby. Upload unstructured data to initialize a simulation sequence.
home.step01Desc: Seed extraction & memory injection & GraphRAG construction
home.step02Desc: Entity extraction & persona generation & Agent config injection
home.step03Desc: Dual-platform parallel sim & auto-parse requirements & temporal memory
home.step04Desc: ReportAgent interacts with the post-simulation environment via rich tools
home.step05Desc: Chat with any simulated individual & converse with ReportAgent
home.promptPlaceholder: // Describe your simulation or prediction requirement in natural language

step1.ontologyDesc: LLM analyzes document content and simulation requirements, extracts reality seeds, and auto-generates a suitable ontology structure
step1.graphRagDesc: Based on the generated ontology, documents are auto-chunked and sent to Zep to build a knowledge graph, extracting entities and relations, forming temporal memory and community summaries
step1.buildCompleteDesc: Graph build is complete. Proceed to the next step for simulation environment setup.

step2.simInstanceDesc: Create a new simulation instance and pull world parameter templates
step2.generateAgentPersonaDesc: Combine context to auto-extract entities and relations from the knowledge graph, initialize simulated individuals, and assign unique behaviors and memories based on reality seeds
step2.dualPlatformConfigDesc: LLM intelligently sets world time flow, recommendation algorithms, each individual's active hours, posting frequency, event triggers, and more based on requirements and reality seeds
step2.initialActivationDesc: Auto-generate initial activation events and hot topics based on narrative direction to guide the simulation world's initial state
step2.setupCompleteDesc: Simulation environment is ready. You can now start the simulation.
step2.roundsConfigDesc: MiroFish auto-plans to simulate {hours} real-world hours, each round representing {minutesPerRound} minutes of elapsed time
step2.customTip: For first-time runs, we strongly recommend switching to 'Custom Mode' to reduce rounds for a quick preview and lower error risk
step2.personaDimExperienceDesc: Complete behavioral trajectory in this event
step2.networkConfigNote: Echo chamber strength sets how strongly agents with the same stance follow each other when the simulation starts. That follow graph decides whose posts each agent sees.

scheduledEvents.title: Scheduled Events
scheduledEvents.desc: Optional posts that you write. A chosen agent publishes each one at the simulated hour you pick; other agents see it from then on. Nothing is invented for you: the generator only suggests, and never adds an event by itself.
scheduledEvents.empty: No scheduled events. The run only uses the initial posts above.
scheduledEvents.contentPlaceholder: What is posted at that hour...
scheduledEvents.suggestedDesc: Hypothetical follow-ups worth testing. They are not part of the run unless you add them.
scheduledEvents.legacyNote: This simulation was prepared with the legacy behavior model, which ignores scheduled events. Prepare it again to use them.

runs.title: Runs
runs.desc: Run the same scenario several times with different random seeds and look at the spread of outcomes instead of a single run. 1 means a single run (the default).
runs.ensembleNote: {runs} independent runs of up to {rounds} rounds each. Cost grows roughly {runs}x; an estimate is shown before anything starts.

step3.oldSimCleared: Old simulation logs cleared, restarting simulation
step3.preparingGoBack: Preparing to return to Step 2, closing simulation...
step3.closeFailed: Failed to close simulation environment, attempting force stop...

step4.panelKeyFacts: Latest key facts from temporal memory

step5.chatWithAgent: Chat with any individual in the world
step5.reportAgentDesc: A conversational version of the report generation agent with access to 4 professional tools and MiroFish's complete memory
step5.toolInsightForgeDesc: Aligns real-world seed data with simulation state, combining Global/Local Memory for cross-temporal deep attribution analysis
step5.toolPanoramaSearchDesc: Graph-based BFS algorithm that reconstructs event propagation paths, capturing the full topology of information flow
step5.toolQuickSearchDesc: GraphRAG-based instant query interface with optimized indexing for fast extraction of node attributes and discrete facts
step5.toolInterviewSubAgentDesc: Autonomous interviews that conduct parallel multi-round dialogues with simulated individuals, collecting unstructured opinion data and psychological states
step5.chatEmptyReportAgent: Chat with Report Agent to explore report content in depth
step5.chatEmptyAgent: Chat with simulated individuals to understand their perspectives
step5.surveyInputPlaceholder: Enter the question you want to ask all selected targets...

kinds.http_402: The provider is refusing requests with HTTP 402: the account is out of credit, or each request asks for more tokens than the budget allows. Agents cannot act until this is fixed. Add credit or switch to another model, then run again.
kinds.http_429: The provider is rate-limiting requests (HTTP 429), so agents skip turns. Use fewer agents or rounds, or a plan with a higher limit.
kinds.auth: The provider rejected the API key (HTTP 401/403). Check LLM_API_KEY in .env and restart the backend.
kinds.http_5xx: The provider is returning server errors (HTTP 5xx). This is usually temporary and the run recovers when it stops.
kinds.timeout: Model requests are timing out. The model may be overloaded or too slow for this many agents.
kinds.connection: The backend cannot reach the model provider. Check your network and LLM_BASE_URL.

resume.title: This run was stopped before it finished
resume.offer: It finished round {round} of {total}. Continue from round {next}, or start over?
resume.memoryNote: Agents' chat memory cannot be restored, so a resumed run will not be identical to an uninterrupted one: agents remember what they saw on the platform, not their earlier reasoning.
resume.inexactNote: This run has no end-of-round checkpoint, so whatever the unfinished round had already done stays on the platform and that round is repeated on top of it.
resume.logOffer: The run stopped after round {round}; it can be resumed.
resume.logResumed: Resumed; the platform databases and logs were kept.
resume.ensembleOffer: {count} run(s) can continue from where they stopped; finished runs are kept.
resume.ensembleRestart: {count} run(s) never got going and will start over.

ensemble.title: Ensemble run
ensemble.reviewDesc: {runs} independent runs of up to {rounds} rounds each, started from the same prepared scenario with different random seeds.
ensemble.seedNote: A seed makes the schedule reproducible (who is active when, reaction delays, who follows whom, scheduled events). It does not make the language model's wording identical, so every run still differs.
ensemble.costBreakdown: {sim} for the simulations and {poll} for the end-of-run questions. This is a conservative upper bound; real usage is usually well below it.
ensemble.questionsDesc: When a run ends, every simulated agent answers these, and the answers are summarised across runs. You can edit them now; they are locked once the runs start.
ensemble.noQuestions: No questions: the runs will only report behaviour metrics (how much, who, when), not what the agents think at the end.
ensemble.questionsInvalid: Every question needs text; choice questions need 2 to 8 different options and number questions need a unit.
ensemble.partialNote: Only {ok} of {total} runs completed. The summary uses those {ok}, so the spread is less reliable.
ensemble.failedNote: Too few runs completed (an ensemble of several runs needs at least 2), so there is nothing to summarise. See the errors above.
ensemble.stoppedNote: The ensemble was stopped before it finished, so there is no summary.
ensemble.caveat: These are distributions of simulated participants' views across {n} stochastic runs, not calibrated probabilities of the real-world event. MiroFish has not been backtested for this domain.
ensemble.meanAbove50: Runs where the agents' mean is above 50

ensemble.fallbackNote: The model could not propose questions for this scenario, so a generic stance question is shown. Edit it, or add your own below, before you start.
